PHOTO TILE (Lantern 1.24.42) -- THIRD INDEPENDENT REVIEW: THE NEWEST PARTS
==========================================================================
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the tile. Date: 2026-11-26.
Build tested: the frozen build photo_r2/index.html (Lantern.version 1.24.42), in headless Chromium (Playwright).
Scope (as asked): layer groups; the PSD reader and writer at 16 and 32 bits (Lr16/Lr32, ZIP with prediction), the
flattened picture of a see-through document, Mac Roman names, Curves with "Crv ", Selective Color; TIFF predictors;
resolution in PNG/JPEG/BMP; the new adjustments' arithmetic; blend modes (Linear Dodge first); Expand/Contract/Border;
the layer styles Satin, Pattern Overlay, Bevel & Emboss, Inner Glow.

Files here
  run_review.py   python3 run_review.py [path/to/index.html] [section ...] [--json cases.json]
                  sections: groups psd tiff dpi adjust blend select fx. One "PASS ..."/"FAIL ..." line a check (and a
                  few "INFO" lines that record without judging), last line "N checks, M failed". A full run takes ~15 s.
  core.py         server, Chromium page, helpers; a .psd writer built by hand from Adobe's Photoshop File Format
                  Specification (16/32-bit, Lr16/Lr32, raw/RLE/ZIP/ZIP-with-prediction), so inputs never come from Lantern.
  pics.py         test pictures (numpy) and CIE Lab by the published formulas.
  sec_*.py        the checks, one file a section.
  inputs/         the TIFFs (written by ImageMagick/libtiff, two by hand from Adobe's TIFF Technical Note 3) and the
                  hand-made .psd files (rewritten on each run, byte for byte the same). 88 KB.
  cases.json      the run as found: 425 checks, 19 failed, plus 8 INFO rows. Each row: what was checked, what Lantern
                  gave, what is right, how that is known, how sure.

References used (never the tile's own comments): psd-tools 1.27 (its reader, and its compositor, whose blend modes and
adjustments say in their comments which readings are pinned against Photoshop's renders), PIL 12, tifffile, ImageMagick
6.9 / libtiff, scipy (exact Euclidean distance transform), numpy; Adobe's PSD spec, TIFF 6.0 and TIFF Technical Note 3,
the PNG and JFIF specifications, W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1, Adobe's Photoshop help text where quoted.
Every hand-made input is first read back by an independent reader ("input check" rows) before Lantern is judged on it.

HOW SURE: "sure" = arithmetic or a published rule, reproduced; "high" = reproduced and an independent program that
claims Photoshop fidelity agrees; "medium" = reproduced, but what Photoshop does is the reviewer's memory or another
program's word.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FAILURES, MOST IMPORTANT FIRST
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. A pass-through group at less than 100% opacity, or with a mask, makes every half see-through pixel under it more
   solid -- even where the group has nothing in it.                                               [sure]
   Steps: a document with no background; a layer whose pixels are half see-through (alpha 128); above it a group
   (Pass Through, Photoshop's usual) at 50% holding a layer that covers only the left half. (Checks "picture: pass-
   through group at 50% opacity over a half see-through picture", "... with a mask over a half see-through picture",
   and the psd-tools-made file "a pass-through group at opacity 100 over a half see-through layer".)
   What happens: on the right half, where the group draws nothing, alpha goes 128 -> 160 (50% opacity) and 128 -> 192
   (a mask, at 100%); with a group at 80% it would be 179. The colour stays; the pixel just gets more solid.
   What is right: 128 -- a group that draws nothing over a pixel changes nothing there. psd-tools interpolates
   between the backdrop and the group's result in premultiplied colour, so the backdrop counts once.
   Why: PHOTO_COMPOSITE drawGroup(), pass-through branch: it copies the canvas (back), draws the group's layers onto it
   (over, which already contains back), then lays over on back by source-over at the group's opacity -- the backdrop is
   laid on itself, and source-over of a half see-through pixel on itself is more solid. A fix that keeps the backdrop
   once: result = back x (1 - k) + over x k in premultiplied terms, k = opacity x mask (e.g. draw back, take k x mask
   out of it with destination-out, then add over, masked and at alpha k, with "lighter").
   Who meets it: anyone making a cut-out, logo or sticker on a transparent background who puts a group at less than
   100% (or masks it): soft edges and shadows under the group thicken, in the PNG and in the .psd's flattened picture,
   and the .psd then looks different in psd-tools/Photoshop than in Lantern. Opaque pictures are not affected.

2. A layer clipped to a soft-edged layer picks up the base layer's own colour along the soft edge.   [high]
   Steps: a soft disc (its edge fades over 4 px) on a picture; a solid layer above it with Clip on. The same at the top
   level, inside a group, and with a group as the base (three checks).
   What happens: at a pixel where the disc is 57% solid, Lantern shows (97,148,163); psd-tools shows (61,201,163),
   which is 57% clipped colour over the picture with none of the disc's colour.
   What is right: Photoshop's clipping mask composites the clipped layers onto the base and then uses the base's
   transparency; psd-tools computes the clipped colour with the base taken as solid, then applies the base's alpha, so
   a solid clipped layer hides the base's colour completely. (Adobe help: "the content of the base layer clips (masks)
   the layers above it".)
   Why: PHOTO_COMPOSITE drawRange(): the clipped layer is cut to the base's alpha (destination-in) and then laid by
   source-over on a canvas that already holds the base, so at a half-solid edge it covers only half of the base. Not
   new code: the first review's clipping test used a hard-edged base, where the two ways agree.
   Who meets it: clipping a colour or texture layer to a soft brush stroke, a feathered cut-out, or anti-aliased text
   leaves a halo of the base's colour round the edge.

3. A flattened .psd with a saved selection (an "Alpha 1" channel) opens see-through, with its colours changed. [high]
   Steps: inputs/flat_with_alpha_channel.psd -- no layers, RGB plus one extra channel, named in image resources 1006
   ("Alpha 1") and 1053 (its id), as Photoshop saves a flattened picture (Background) with a saved selection.
   What happens: the saved selection is used as transparency (alpha 0 to 253) and the colours are "un-matted" from
   white (colour off by up to 226).
   What is right: a solid picture with its colours as stored; the extra channel is a selection, not transparency (a
   Background has none). psd-tools reads it so (its has_transparency() looks for a Mtrn/Mt16/Mt32 block or a negative
   layer count, and treats channels named in 1053 as saved alpha channels).
   Why: PHOTO_PSD_READ read(): "if (nch > base && !layers.length) planes[-1] = planes[base]" takes any extra channel
   of a layerless file as transparency, and the new un-matting then follows it. Suggest: take it as transparency only
   when the file says so (Mtrn/Mt16/Mt32, or a negative layer count), not when resources 1006/1053 name alpha channels.
   Who meets it: print and product-photo work, where flattened PSDs with saved clipping selections are common.

4. 32-bit .psd: transparency and layer masks are put through the sRGB colour curve.                  [sure]
   Steps: inputs/lr32_c0.psd (alpha 0.5 at one pixel), a 32-bit layer with a layer mask of 0.5, and a layerless 32-bit
   file with an alpha channel (three checks).
   What happens: alpha 0.5 -> 188 (74% solid), mask 0.5 -> 188, layerless alpha 127/255 -> 187.
   What is right: 128. Alpha and masks are coverage, never gamma-encoded; psd-tools reads all three as 0.5.
   Why: PHOTO_PSD_READ to8() applies the linear-to-sRGB curve to every 32-bit channel, alpha (-1), masks (-2/-3) and
   the flattened picture's alpha included. Colour channels are a separate question (finding 6).

5. Hue/Saturation with a colour range (Reds, Blues ...) changes the Lightness of near-greys fully.      [high]
   Steps: Hue/Saturation, Blues, Lightness -50, on (250,250,255) (white with a faint cool cast) and other near-greys;
   Reds, Lightness +60, on (180,178,178).
   What happens: (250,250,255) -> (125,125,128); (200,200,205) -> (100,100,103); (180,178,178) -> (225,224,224).
   What is right: a few levels at most. psd-tools (its model fitted to Photoshop's renders) gives (249,249,252),
   (199,199,202) and (180,179,179): a range's Lightness is scaled by how saturated the pixel is, so greys stay grey.
   Why: PHOTO_ADJ_COLOR hueSat(): a range's weight is taken in full whenever the pixel's saturation is above 0
   ("if (w && hh[1] > 0)"), and light() then moves the colour toward black or white by the whole amount.
   Who meets it: darkening a blue sky with Blues -50 also turns white clouds, paper and snow with a slight blue cast
   grey; brightening Reds lifts warm greys and skin shadows. (The range's Hue and Saturation are not affected the
   same way: they act through the pixel's own saturation.)

6. A 32-bit float means different things in a TIFF and in a PSD.                    [sure they differ; unsure which is right]
   0.5 opens as 128 from a 32-bit TIFF and as 188 from a 32-bit PSD; 0.21404 as 55 and 128. PHOTO_TIFF sample()
   multiplies by 255 (as libtiff/ImageMagick do); PHOTO_PSD_READ to8() applies the sRGB curve (as a display of
   Photoshop's linear 32-bit documents would). Either may be defended; one picture should not come out two ways.

7. Inner Glow size 0 draws a size-10 glow; Bevel & Emboss size 0 draws a size-5 bevel.                [medium]
   The tile's own sliders offer 0 to 250. At 0 Lantern's picture is exactly the one size 10 (glow) or size 5 (bevel)
   gives. In Photoshop the Size is how far the effect reaches in from the edge; at 0 it shows nothing (reviewer's
   memory). Why: PHOTO_FX apply(): "e.size || 10" and "Math.max(1, e.size || 5)" read 0 as missing.

8. A camera JPEG (resolution only in its EXIF, no JFIF segment) opens at 72 ppi.                     [medium]
   A JPEG with EXIF XResolution/YResolution 300, ResolutionUnit inches (as cameras write), no APP0: Lantern 72; PIL
   reads 300. PHOTO_FILES dpiIn() reads JFIF only, and only when the APP0 segment comes straight after the start
   marker. Photoshop takes such a file's resolution from EXIF (reviewer's memory). Saving then stamps 72 into the copy.

9. A 32-bit float TIFF with the horizontal predictor (2) opens as wrong pixels, without a word.          [sure]
   inputs/t32_zip_p2.tif (ImageMagick/libtiff; libtiff reads it back exactly). Lantern: every pixel after the first
   of a row is wrong (e.g. (29,0,0) for (29,103,177)). PHOTO_TIFF read() undoes predictor 2 only at 8 and 16 bits.
   It should undo it on the 32-bit words too, or refuse the file plainly. Rare (most float TIFFs use predictor 3).

10. Vivid Light with a pure black or pure white source.                                              [medium]
   White (255) over black (0): Lantern 0, psd-tools 255; black over white: Lantern 255, psd-tools 0. psd-tools says
   "inside Vivid Light the source extreme wins ... pinned against Photoshop's own render (#189)". Lantern takes the
   backdrop's special cases of Color Dodge/Burn (PHOTO_BLEND burn()/dodge()). Not seen in Photoshop by this reviewer.

11. Undo of a later step reopens a group that was shut by hand.                                       [medium]
   Shut a group (toggleGroup, rightly not a History step), do anything else, Undo: the group is open again, because the
   History states keep each layer's open flag. In Photoshop, opening and shutting groups is outside History (memory).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORDED, NOT JUDGED (the sources disagree, or Photoshop's behaviour is not known to the reviewer)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Hard Mix where backdrop + source = 255 exactly: Lantern gives 255 (Adobe's help: "255 or greater ... 255");
  psd-tools gives 0 unless the backdrop is above half, saying Photoshop's renders do so (#189).
- A group clipped to the layer below: Lantern clips it and saves the flag; psd-tools ignores a group's clipping flag
  ("In Photoshop, clipping groups are not supported"), so other programs may show the group unclipped.
- Expand on a feathered selection makes its edge hard (255 out to the 50% line + r, then 0): the feather is lost.
  Whether Photoshop keeps the feather is not known to the reviewer.
- Legacy Brightness/Contrast at contrast 100: input 127 -> 0 (psd-tools 127, its line at an infinite slope); every
  other setting tried matches psd-tools within 1.
- Hue/Saturation colour ranges otherwise against psd-tools' fitted model: Reds hue+30/sat+40 within 5 (mean 0.6),
  Greens sat -100 within 2; only the Lightness on near-greys (finding 5) is far off.
- Pattern Overlay with no pattern defined yet leaves the layer as it was and says nothing (the dialog's label says to
  define one first).
- From reading the writer, not a check: a non-ASCII layer name's Pascal (old) name is written with one "?" for each
  UTF-8 byte ("Café" -> "Caf??"); readers use the Unicode name (luni), which is right, so only programs that ignore
  luni see it.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT WAS RIGHT (briefly)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Groups: 21 of 26 grouped pictures match psd-tools' compositor on the .psd Lantern saves, within 4 levels: pass-through
  and Normal groups with Multiply/Screen/Overlay layers inside, groups in Multiply/Difference/Hard Light, group
  opacity over opaque pictures, group masks over opaque pictures, nested groups (three pass-through levels at 70%),
  hidden groups and hidden layers, Invert/Levels/Curves adjustment layers inside pass-through groups (changing what is
  under) and inside Normal groups (changing only the group), a layer clipped to a pass-through group, empty groups.
  The saved tree (names in Unicode, nesting, modes, opacity, eyes, open/shut) is what psd-tools reads, also for 30
  random trees up to four deep, and Lantern reopens its own files to the same tree. psd-tools-made grouped files open
  with the same tree and the same picture (4 of 5; the fifth is finding 1).
  Group Layers (one layer, a range holding a group; refuses a range that is not side by side), New Group (empty, saved
  empty), Ungroup (nested: one level up; picture kept), Merge Group (five kinds: picture kept), toggle open/shut (no
  History step, saved shut), Delete group (with its layers), Duplicate nested group (the copies belong to the copies,
  pixels independent, saved as two whole groups), Move Layer into an open group / over a shut one / out at the top and
  bottom / a whole group up and down, the tree whole after every move of 30 random trees, every move undone by the
  opposite move, the Move tool moving a whole group, Merge Visible and Merge Down with groups, Undo and Redo of seven
  group commands (tree and picture exact).
PSD: 16-bit files with layers in Lr16 (raw, ZIP, ZIP with prediction): values exactly round(v/257), places, a group,
  a multiply layer at opacity 200, Mac Roman name. 32-bit Lr32: raw, ZIP and ZIP-with-prediction give the same
  pixels (psd-tools decodes the same hand-made bytes to the same floats). Layerless see-through 8- and 16-bit files:
  the white taken off again (within 1.5 on colour x alpha). Lantern's own flattened picture: laid over white with its
  alpha channel, as psd-tools expects. Mac Roman names: all 128 high bytes as Apple's table (Python's mac_roman, the
  euro at 0xDB); luni preferred. Curves: written with both the old section and "Crv " (psd-tools reads the same points
  in both, three cases, and composites as Lantern shows within 3); a hand-made Curves layer opens live. Selective
  Color: relative and absolute written as Adobe's spec (first record zero, values clamped to +-100), psd-tools reads
  them, Lantern reopens them; a hand-made one with a junk first record opens right. Hue/Saturation (master and
  Colorize) and legacy Brightness/Contrast blocks read by psd-tools with the same settings.
TIFF: 16-bit with the horizontal predictor: LZW and Deflate, little and big endian, chunky and planar, several strips,
  16x16 tiles, grey and RGBA: exactly round(v/257) (RGBA within 1.5 on colour x alpha). 32-bit float with the
  floating-point predictor: Deflate and LZW (libtiff's), and by hand per Technical Note 3 (grey in 2-row strips; RGBA
  big-endian with alpha 0.5): all within 1 of round(v x 255); uncompressed float too.
Resolution: PNG (one pHYs before IDAT, right CRC), JPEG (one JFIF, dots per inch), BMP (pixels per metre) and TIFF at
  72, 72.5, 96, 150, 300, 600 ppi: PIL reads them back. Opening PIL's PNG/JPEG/BMP at 96, 240, 300: right (96.01 from a
  PNG, which holds whole pixels per metre); pHYs unit 0 -> 72; JFIF in dots/cm -> 299.72. A 300 ppi PNG saved as PNG,
  JPEG, BMP, TIFF and PSD stays 300.
Adjustments: Hue/Saturation master hue/saturation/lightness and Colorize, 17 settings, match psd-tools within 3;
  neutral changes nothing; saturation -100 gives the HSL-lightness grey; lightness +-100 white/black; greys stay grey;
  alpha kept. Legacy Brightness/Contrast, 8 settings, within 1 of psd-tools. Shadows/Highlights: 0/0 changes nothing,
  alpha kept, greys stay grey, shadows lift only the dark half, highlights darken only the light half, hues kept,
  1 x 1 works. Match Color: no source changes nothing (within 1), Fade 100 changes nothing, matched picture takes the
  source's Lab mean and spread (Reinhard), Neutralize removes a cast, alpha kept, a fully clear picture is left alone.
  Replace Color: neutral changes nothing, colours beyond the fuzziness untouched, alpha kept, hue +120 turns the red
  green. Selective Color: neutral changes nothing; each colour range leaves greys and the far colours untouched;
  Adobe's own example right (50% + 10%: 55% relative, 60% absolute); relative cannot change pure white; absolute
  whites cyan +50 gives 50% cyan; black (K) keeps greys grey; alpha kept; Reds magenta -100% makes red yellow.
Blend modes: Linear Dodge (Add) at 100, 70, 50, 25% over solid and see-through backdrops matches min(1, b + s) laid on
  by source-over (W3C 5.1) within 2, alpha as source-over's. All 26 other modes match psd-tools on every value pair
  with both layers solid (within 2, three known disagreements set aside) and, at 100% and 70% over see-through
  layers, on every pixel that is not on a knife edge (pixels whose blend jumps by more than 4 levels when a colour
  moves 2 levels -- the canvas keeps a see-through colour only to about that -- are left out and counted in each
  check's name). Dissolve: every pixel wholly source or backdrop, in proportion to the opacity.
Selections: Expand by 1, 3, 10 of a rectangle, disc, ring and one pixel takes every pixel within r and nothing past
  r + 1 (scipy's exact distance); straight edges move exactly r, hard; one pixel by 3 gives the 29 pixels. Contract
  likewise; a too-big contract leaves no selection and no error. Expand 4 then Contract 4 gives the rectangle back.
  Border 4, 7, 10: a band astride the edge, as wide as asked, nothing past it. The menu command equals the function.
Layer styles: Satin, Pattern Overlay, Bevel & Emboss and Inner Glow at their defaults and at sizes 0, 1, 250 and 5000,
  distances 0 and 250, depths 1 and 1000, altitudes 0 and 90, scales 1 and 1000: no error and the layer's alpha
  exactly kept (the soft edge too), each visibly changing the inside at its defaults. Pattern Overlay tiles the
  defined pattern from the document's corner exactly. All four on a 1 x 1 document, an empty layer, a 300 x 1 half
  see-through line, together, and on a group: no error, alpha kept.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT COULD NOT BE TESTED
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Photoshop itself. Where Photoshop's behaviour is named it is psd-tools' word (its comments say which readings are
  pinned against Photoshop's renders) or the reviewer's memory, marked so.
- Satin, Bevel & Emboss, Inner Glow and Pattern Overlay against any renderer: psd-tools draws none of them, so they
  were judged only by the rules (inside only, alpha kept, no breakage), not by how they look.
- Selective Color, Shadows/Highlights and Match Color against Photoshop's own numbers (proprietary; psd-tools has
  none of them); they were held to the published examples and to rules.
- Big pictures and speed: every input is small (at most 100 x 7 for the blend grid, 60 x 40 for selections).
- 16-bit PSD channels packed with PackBits (the hand-made writer packs PackBits at 8 bits only); 32-bit float TIFF
  with LZW in big-endian order (ImageMagick 6.9 wrote files that libtiff itself reads back as zeros, so they could not
  serve as inputs; big-endian float with the predictor was tested with a hand-made Deflate file instead).
- Group commands through the menus, keys and Layers panel: the commands were run through Lantern.photo.ops.exec only
  (the second review drove the panel by clicks).
